name: Butthole Surfers
label: Touch and Go
lede: A Trinity University Accountant of the Year and an MBA student bought stolen strobe lights, toured with a naked dancer, made some of the strangest records of the eighties, then sued their own label and won.

eras.title: The accountant quits
eras.text: Gibby Haynes and Paul Leary were headed for business careers when a fake medical magazine got in the way. They changed the band's name every show until an emcee picked one for them, and a short set in San Francisco turned into a record deal.

years.h: Strange V.D. gets Gibby Haynes out of accounting
years.p: Haynes, a Trinity University basketball captain and Accountant of the Year, and MBA student Paul Leary make a magazine of medical photos with invented captions. He is caught with a copy at his accounting firm and leaves.
years.xp: Haynes moved to Southern California and Leary, one semester short of his degree, followed. They sold homemade clothing printed with Lee Harvey Oswald's face before heading back to San Antonio to start a band.

years.h: An emcee forgets the band's name and uses a song title
years.p: At their first paid show, at the Bonham Exchange in San Antonio, the emcee introduces Gibby Haynes and Paul Leary by the title of their song Butthole Surfer. They keep it.
years.xp:
Before that they used a new name every show. Haynes lists the Dick Clark Five, the Vodka Family Winstons, the Ashtray Babyheads and Ed Asner Is Gay among them.

Clubs, newspapers and radio stations spent the next two decades refusing to print or say the real name, calling them B.H. Surfers instead.

years.h: Jello Biafra catches a short set and offers them a record
years.p: The band has moved to California in a van. At San Francisco's Tool and Die, [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] of [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]] offers to put out a record on Alternative Tentacles if they can book the studio time.

years.h: The Mathews brothers quit after a fight with Gibby Haynes
years.p: Bassist Quinn Mathews and drummer Scott Mathews leave after a physical fight between Scott and Haynes. [[King Coffey|f275d56b-3601-476f-a4bf-b50892750984]] becomes the band's permanent drummer.

years.h: Butthole Surfers EP, a.k.a. Pee Pee the Sailor · Alternative Tentacles
years.p: Cut at BOSS Studios in San Antonio, with The Shah Sleeps in Lee Harvey's Grave and Bar-B-Q Pope. [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] listed it among his ten favorite albums in his journals.
play: The Shah Sleeps in Lee Harvey's Grave

years.h: Teresa Nervosa makes it two drummers
years.p: [[Teresa Taylor|4e998ae8-008c-4e85-8415-7903e9c4e265]], as Teresa Nervosa, joins to play alongside Coffey. They drum in unison on stand-up kits and are billed as siblings, though they're not related.

eras.title: Stolen strobes and a studio hostage
eras.text: A studio owner held their first album hostage, so Alternative Tentacles released a live EP and Touch and Go got the album. On the road, the band became the show people warned each other about.

years.h: Bob O'Neill keeps the tapes until somebody pays
years.p: O'Neill, who owns BOSS Studios, won't release the band's 1984 masters until he's paid, and Alternative Tentacles can't pay. The label puts out the live EP Live PCPPEP instead.

years.h: Psychic... Powerless... Another Man's Sac · Touch and Go
years.p: Booking agent Terry Tolkin brings the band to [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]], and Touch and Go puts out their first album. It includes Butthole Surfer, the song that named them.

years.cap: Butthole Surfers at Chasers, Greensboro, North Carolina
years.h: The band buys stolen strobe lights at a bargain
years.p: Reported as several thousand dollars' worth. Soon the lights take up more room than the instruments.
years.xp:
They projected films behind them, often upside down or backwards: car crashes, nuclear blasts, meat processing and penis reconstruction surgery, plus a color negative of a Charlie's Angels episode. The strobes and films occasionally gave audience members seizures.

Gibby Haynes wore hundreds of clothespins, stripped down as the show went on, burst condoms full of stage blood and set a cymbal full of lighter fluid on fire, sometimes along with his hand.

years.h: Kramer of Shockabilly gets the bass call before Europe
years.p: Terence Smart quits after falling in love, Canadian Trevor Malcolm quits in mid-1985 and Juan Molina fills in for one tour. Then the band phones [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]], who says yes.

years.h: Worn out, Teresa Nervosa leaves after a Christmas tour of Europe
years.p: Drummer Kytha Gernatt, known as Cabbage, fills in. Touch and Go releases the Cream Corn from the Socket of Davis EP.

eras.title: A naked dancer and a burning cymbal
eras.text: The classic line-up came together in 1986 and lived in Georgia, then on a ranch outside Austin. The shows got wilder, and the three Touch and Go albums are the ones fans rank highest.

years.h: Rembrandt Pussyhorse, the album Alternative Tentacles passed on
years.p: Alternative Tentacles sat on it for about a year, then turned it down. Touch and Go released a re-recorded version, with a minimal rework of the Guess Who's American Woman.

yt: Live at CBGB, New York, February 1986
years.h: Jeff Pinkus replaces Kramer and the classic line-up locks in
years.p: [[Jeff Pinkus|e72f5512-49b1-498f-98ff-26e3e39322aa]] takes the bass and holds it until 1994. Teresa Nervosa comes back and Cabbage is fired.

years.cap: Butthole Surfers at Chasers, Greensboro, North Carolina, 1986
years.h: Kathleen Lynch meets the band at Sex World and stays
years.p: She is working at a New York strip club called Sex World when they meet. She never becomes an official member, but she dances with them, naked, through 1989.
years.xp: At a Washington, D.C. show with [[Gwar|f7ccd53a-234c-4800-8d1b-21b201bad1de]] she danced in nothing but gold body paint and antique wooden snowshoes. She went by the name Ta-Da the Shit Lady.

years.cap: Gibby Haynes onstage at Chasers, Greensboro, North Carolina, 1986
years.h: A 1986 show ends with a small fire and a screwdriver
years.p: After five songs Gibby Haynes starts a small fire, and Paul Leary takes a screwdriver to the club's speakers.
years.xp: According to Michael Azerrad's Our Band Could Be Your Life, as summarized by Wikipedia, Haynes and Kathleen Lynch, both shaved bald by then, reportedly had sex onstage that night.

years.h: Locust Abortion Technician · Touch and Go
years.p: Cut on cheap gear in a rented house in Winterville, Georgia. It opens with Sweat Loaf, a warped take on Black Sabbath's Sweet Leaf, under Arthur Sarnoff's painting of two clowns and a dog.
years.xp: Leary said the bad equipment forced them to be more creative. Kurt Cobain put it in his top 50 albums, and it reached No. 3 on the UK indie chart. Around its release the band bought a ranch house on five acres in Driftwood, Texas, about 30 miles from Austin, and turned it into a studio.

years.h: Hairway to Steven names no songs, just draws them
years.p: Cut in a week in January 1988 at January Sound in Dallas. The title spoonerizes Led Zeppelin's Stairway to Heaven, and each song gets a crude cartoon in place of a name.
years.xp: Fans later matched the songs to titles using the 1989 Double Live album. It was Teresa Nervosa's last studio album with the band. Jeff Pinkus later said the faster, tidier sessions stifled some of their spontaneity.

years.h: Bar-B-Que Movie spoofs The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
years.p: Tom Stern and [[Alex Winter|28e5288b-1c6e-4b89-961c-287d5868ced9]] of Bill & Ted shoot a Super 8 short that ends with the band, Kathleen Lynch and a burning cymbal playing the song Fast.

years.h: Double Live answers the bootleggers
years.p: Recorded on a portable DAT on the winter 1988 tour, it is the first release on the band's own Latino Buggerveil label.

years.h: Teresa Nervosa leaves for good, then needs brain surgery
years.p: Soon after quitting, Teresa Taylor is diagnosed with an aneurysm. Surgery leaves her with seizures set off by strobe lights.
years.xp: After the Widowermaker EP, their last Touch and Go release, the band left for Rough Trade. Kathleen Lynch stopped dancing with them the same year, and the shows became more predictable.

eras.title: Signed to the Beatles' label, sued the indie
eras.text: The band that couldn't get its name in a newspaper signed to the Beatles' old label and had a No. 1 modern rock hit. Then it sued Touch and Go over a handshake deal, and the indie world took sides.

years.h: Piouhgd lands badly, then Lollapalooza calls
years.p: The title is pronounced "pissed off." Critics are disappointed, and Gibby Haynes and Paul Leary later disown it, but the band still gets a slot on the first Lollapalooza that summer. Rough Trade goes bankrupt.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the April 1991 record leaned on more electronic instrumentation and was largely viewed as a disappointment next to their earlier work.

years.h: Kurt Cobain meets Courtney Love at a Butthole Surfers show
years.p: Cobain and Love meet at a show with [[L7|57111f1f-9829-45ea-bb4e-a5aba37cd1d1]] on the bill, according to Wikipedia.

q: A lot of people gave us grief for doing that.
years.h: Independent Worm Saloon, produced by John Paul Jones · Capitol
years.p: Signed to Capitol in 1992, the band works with Led Zeppelin's [[John Paul Jones|4490113a-3880-4f5b-a39b-105bfceaed04]]. Who Was in My Room Last Night? is their first radio hit.
years.xp: Leary said in 2017 that being on the Beatles' and Dean Martin's label felt too weird to turn down. Wikipedia says the single reached No. 24 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart and the album No. 124 on the Billboard 200.
play: Who Was in My Room Last Night?

years.h: Gibby Haynes is on stage at the Viper Room when River Phoenix dies
years.p: Haynes is playing the Los Angeles club with P, his band with Johnny Depp, the night the actor dies of a drug overdose there.
years.xp: Wikipedia, drawing on Leary and industry insiders, says Haynes was increasingly dependent on hard drugs in this period; Haynes downplayed their concern. P released one album on Capitol in 1995.

years.h: Jeff Pinkus quits after eight years on bass
years.p: Gibby Haynes, Paul Leary and King Coffey carry on with fill-ins. Leary builds a producing career and Coffey runs his label, Trance Syndicate.

years.src: AV Club · Walthal v. Rusk · Wikipedia
years.h: The Butthole Surfers take their own label to federal court
years.p: Paul Leary on why the band sued Touch and Go in December 1995. They had no contract, only a 50-50 split, and Corey Rusk wouldn't raise their royalties or return the masters.
years.xp:
A district court sided with the band in early 1998 and the Seventh Circuit affirmed in March 1999. Leary said Touch and Go's objection to a bigger royalty "incensed us a little bit because we felt like we were floating the Touch And Go boat." On Rusk's claim to the catalog: "If he really wanted to own us for life, he should have gotten that on paper."

[[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] was among the peers who criticized the band for suing. Asked about Rusk, he said "I can't speak highly enough of Corey Rusk. He's a straight shooter." Haynes answered that Rusk sent accounting statements nobody could understand.

The band reissued their Touch and Go albums on Latino Buggerveil, and Touch and Go started asking bands to sign a memorandum of intent instead of shaking hands.

years.h: Electriclarryland turns Pepper into a No. 1 hit
years.p: Pepper tops Billboard's Modern Rock chart and the album reaches No. 31 on the Billboard 200. Butthole Surfers songs also land in Romeo + Juliet and Beavis and Butt-Head Do America.

years.h: Capitol shelves After the Astronaut
years.p: The follow-up to Electriclarryland is scrapped as relations with Capitol sour, and the band splits bitterly with manager Tom Bunch.

eras.title: Free of Capitol, one more lap
eras.text: The band remade its shelved album for Hollywood Records and went quiet. In 2008 the classic line-up, Teresa Nervosa included, toured again for two years.

years.h: Weird Revolution recycles the shelved album · Hollywood/Surfdog
years.p: Most of the After the Astronaut songs return, re-recorded and pushed toward electronics and hip-hop. The Shame of Life reaches No. 24 on the Modern Rock chart.

years.cap: Butthole Surfers in Minehead, England, December 2008
years.h: The 1986-89 line-up tours again
years.p: Jeff Pinkus and Teresa Nervosa rejoin Gibby Haynes, Paul Leary and King Coffey for the East Coast and Europe, the first shows by that line-up since 1989.
years.xp: An appearance at All Tomorrow's Parties ended in a dispute with festival founder Barry Hogan, who told a reporter the band would never play there again.

years.cap: Butthole Surfers at the Fillmore, San Francisco, New Year's 2009
years.h: "This may be our last," Gibby Haynes tells Austin
years.p: At the last scheduled North American date of the reunion tour, Haynes reminds the crowd that the band played its first show as the Butthole Surfers in Austin.
years.xp: His words, as Wikipedia prints them: "We played our first show as the Butthole Surfers in Austin. And this may be our last."

eras.title: The hole truth
eras.text: The touring mostly stopped. A book, a documentary and a Stranger Things sync kept the band in the news, Teresa Taylor died in 2023, and the album Capitol shelved got a release date.

years.cap: Butthole Surfers at the Day for Night festival, Houston, December 2016
years.h: Paul Leary is done touring
years.p: With the band on hiatus, he says the hour onstage is fun and the other 23 hours are not.

years.h: Aaron Tanner's What Does Regret Mean? puts the flyers in a book
years.p: The coffee-table visual history collects the band's flyers, photos and art.

years.h: Teresa Taylor dies at 60
years.p: Taylor, who drummed as Teresa Nervosa, dies of lung disease she'd made public in 2021. The band posts that she passed away peacefully. Rolling Stone notes her 1991 cameo in Richard Linklater's Slacker put her on the film's poster.

years.h: The Hole Truth and Nothing Butt premieres in Austin
years.p: Tom Stern's documentary about the band plays the Paramount Theatre during South by Southwest.

years.h: Four Butthole Surfers play Los Angeles after the documentary
years.p: After the film's West Coast premiere, Gibby Haynes, Paul Leary, King Coffey and Jeff Pinkus play a short set at the Egyptian Theatre, their first as the Butthole Surfers since October 2017.

years.h: Human Cannonball turns up in Stranger Things
years.p: The Locust Abortion Technician song plays in Chapter 7 of the show's fifth season.

years.h: After the Astronaut finally gets a release date
years.p: Announced March 17 with the single Jet Fighter, the album the band made after Electriclarryland is set for release on Sunset Blvd Records.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: Teresa Taylor dead at 60
